normalized.title: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
normalized.description: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

normalized.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a mechanism for an optical ground station that can adjust the beam's divergence during the link sessionwithout link interruption and whilst maintaining the optical pointing accuracy.TargetedImprovements:To enable dynamic adjustment of the beam divergence without needing optical realignment. Eventually, integrating the beacon capabilities with the communications beam.Description: Alignment of the optical system at an optical ground station is usually needed before a link session, especially if the optical configuration (beam divergence)has changed. It is essential that for links targeting optical feeder applications the ground-space connectivity must be maintained.Furthermore, ground-to-space links usually make use of a beacon during the acquisition phase. normalized.title: S3-CL-03 ERASE PHASE A ACTIVE DEBRIS REMOVAL MISSION FOR LARGE UNPREPARED LEO PLATFORMS - EXPRO+
normalized.description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry.  The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the  Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

normalized.title: S2-SW-10: CANADIAN PARTICIPATION IN THE ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK FEASIBILITY STUDY
normalized.description: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.

normalized.title: PRESERVATION ASSETS OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE SERVICE (PAOM-SER)
normalized.description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. The generation of thematic collections and geographical datasets has further enhanced their usability and value.The Preservation Assets Operations and Maintenance (PAOM) Service will:Operate, maintain, and evolve Space Data Preservation System (SDPS) assets located at ESRIN;Manage the ESRIN EO Legacy Media Archive and Transcription Chains and perform legacy media transcription and data recovery;Generate thematic collections and geographical coverages using heritage data;Manage the ESRIN laboratory activities in support to transcription chains set-up and Philab Air Quality Platform activities, and manage and maintain the ESRIN AF Antenna;Support local visits at the Heritage Missions Walkthrough and Memorabilia Wall located at ESRIN and heritage missionsrelated outreach activities.

normalized.title: NAVISP EL1-132 DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF FLEXIBLE ELORAN/GNSS SIGNAL SIMULATOR- EXPRO+
normalized.description: The increasing dependence on GNSS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services has highlighted vulnerabilities to jamming,spoofing, interference and space-weather effects. eLORAN is emerging as a resilient terrestrial complement to GNSS, but its adoptionrequires advanced tools capable of realistically testing and validating hybrid GNSS/eLORAN solutions. normalized.description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. normalized.title: PHASED ARRAYS EXPLOITING GRATING LOBESFOR SCATTEROMETER INSTRUMENTS EXPRO PLUS
normalized.description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.

normalized.title: NAVISP-EL1-131-CHIP SCALE OPTICAL ATOMIC CLOCK FOR PNT APPLICATIONS EXPRO+ REISSUE OF (1-13610)
normalized.description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.
